Map each node in the provided diagram to the source code that implements or explains it.

Read each label in the context of its branch. A node can stand for a single fact, a component, or a flow. Follow it into the source until the code covers what the label describes. When a label names a function, type, or file, include its full declaration. Favor complete coverage over tight ranges; extra surrounding lines are fine, and precision is reviewed in a later step. A node can have several ranges across files.

For large diagrams, assign subtrees to subagents. Each subagent returns mappings for its own nodes. Combine them into one candidate, map any remaining nodes, then validate and submit it yourself. You decide whether and how to split. Use delegate_subagents with several assignments in one call to run them in parallel.

Inputs: the AgentContext contains the pinned, read-only repository checkout and diagram-data.json (ASCII and node references). No layout template or external reference examples are provided. Do not change diagram text or layout.

Output: return only JSON in this form:
{"diagrams":[{"diagramId":"d1","mappings":[{"node":"n1","path":"relative/file.ts","startLine":10,"endLine":20}]}],"notes":"Unsupported nodes or uncertainty"}
Each entry is one repository-relative, 1-based, inclusive range; repeat a node for multiple ranges. Include every diagram. If you can't support a node, leave it unmapped and say why in notes.

Read ranges with per-file line numbers (for example, nl -ba file) rather than inferring them from search hits. Before returning, call validate_source_mappings with your complete candidate and fix any errors. Your final JSON must match a candidate that passed.

If you receive a subagent assignment, map only the assigned nodes and return their partial mappings and notes using the same JSON shape. You have read/bash tools only; the main agent handles delegation, remaining nodes, validation and final submission.

Subagent assignment (child-output):
Map n38-n54 and n87-n90, n96, output parsing, exec, resize. Return JSON partial.

1	//! Primary terminal IO ("termio") state. This maintains the terminal state,
     2	//! pty, subprocess, etc. This is flexible enough to be used in environments
     3	//! that don't have a pty and simply provides the input/output using raw
     4	//! bytes.
     5	pub const Termio = @This();
     6	
     7	const std = @import("std");
     8	const assert = @import("../quirks.zig").inlineAssert;
     9	const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator;
    10	const ArenaAllocator = std.heap.ArenaAllocator;
    11	const EnvMap = std.process.Environ.Map;
    12	const posix = std.posix;
    13	const termio = @import("../termio.zig");
    14	const StreamHandler = @import("stream_handler.zig").StreamHandler;
    15	const terminalpkg = @import("../terminal/main.zig");
    16	const global = @import("../global.zig");
    17	const xev = global.xev;
    18	const renderer = @import("../renderer.zig");
    19	const apprt = @import("../apprt.zig");
    20	const internal_os = @import("../os/main.zig");
    21	const windows = internal_os.windows;
    22	const configpkg = @import("../config.zig");
    23	const ProcessInfo = @import("../pty.zig").ProcessInfo;
    24	const compat_file = @import("../lib/compat/file.zig");
    25	
    26	const log = std.log.scoped(.io_exec);
    27	
    28	/// Mutex state argument for queueMessage.
    29	pub const MutexState = enum { locked, unlocked };
    30	
    31	/// Allocator
    32	alloc: Allocator,
    33	
    34	/// This is the implementation responsible for io.
    35	backend: termio.Backend,
    36	
    37	/// The derived configuration for this termio implementation.
    38	config: DerivedConfig,
    39	
    40	/// The terminal emulator internal state. This is the abstract "terminal"
    41	/// that manages input, grid updating, etc. and is renderer-agnostic. It
    42	/// just stores internal state about a grid.
    43	terminal: terminalpkg.Terminal,
    44	
    45	/// The shared render state
    46	renderer_state: *renderer.State,
    47	
    48	/// A handle to wake up the renderer. This hints to the renderer that
    49	/// a repaint should happen.
    50	renderer_wakeup: xev.Async,
    51	
    52	/// The mailbox for notifying the renderer of things.
    53	renderer_mailbox: *renderer.Thread.Mailbox,
    54	
    55	/// The mailbox for communicating with the surface.
    56	surface_mailbox: apprt.surface.Mailbox,
    57	
    58	/// The cached size info
    59	size: renderer.Size,
    60	
    61	/// The mailbox implementation to use.
    62	mailbox: termio.Mailbox,
    63	
    64	/// The stream parser. This parses the stream of escape codes and so on
    65	/// from the child process and calls callbacks in the stream handler.
    66	terminal_stream: StreamHandler.Stream,
    67	
    68	/// Last time the cursor was reset. This is used to prevent message
    69	/// flooding with cursor resets.
    70	last_cursor_reset: ?std.Io.Timestamp = null,
    71	
    72	/// State we have for thread enter. This may be null if we don't need
    73	/// to keep track of any state or if its already been freed.
    74	thread_enter_state: ?*ThreadEnterState = null,
    75	
    76	/// The state we need to keep around only until we enter the IO
    77	/// thread. Then we can throw it all away.
    78	const ThreadEnterState = struct {
    79	    arena: ArenaAllocator,
    80	
    81	    /// Initial input to send to the subprocess after starting. This
    82	    /// memory is freed once the subprocess start is attempted, even
    83	    /// if it fails, because Exec only starts once.
    84	    input: configpkg.io.RepeatableReadableIO,
    85	
    86	    pub fn create(
    87	        alloc: Allocator,
    88	        config: *const configpkg.Config,
    89	    ) !?*ThreadEnterState {
    90	        // If we have no input then we have no thread enter state
    91	        if (config.input.list.items.len == 0) return null;
    92	
    93	        // Create our arena allocator
    94	        var arena = ArenaAllocator.init(alloc);
    95	        errdefer arena.deinit();
    96	        const arena_alloc = arena.allocator();
    97

20	/// stateful and is expected to live for the entire lifetime of the terminal.
    21	/// It is NOT VALID to stop a stream handler, create a new one, and use that
    22	/// unless all of the member fields are copied.
    23	pub const StreamHandler = struct {
    24	    alloc: Allocator,
    25	    size: *renderer.Size,
    26	    terminal: *terminal.Terminal,
    27	
    28	    /// Mailbox for data to the termio thread.
    29	    termio_mailbox: *termio.Mailbox,
    30	
    31	    /// Mailbox for the surface.
    32	    surface_mailbox: apprt.surface.Mailbox,
    33	
    34	    /// The shared render state
    35	    renderer_state: *renderer.State,
    36	
    37	    /// The mailbox for notifying the renderer of things.
    38	    renderer_mailbox: *renderer.Thread.Mailbox,
    39	
    40	    /// A handle to wake up the renderer. This hints to the renderer that
    41	    /// a repaint should happen.
    42	    renderer_wakeup: xev.Async,
    43	
    44	    /// The response to use for ENQ requests. The memory is owned by
    45	    /// whoever owns StreamHandler.
    46	    enquiry_response: []const u8,
    47	
    48	    /// The color reporting format for OSC requests.
    49	    osc_color_report_format: configpkg.Config.OSCColorReportFormat,
    50	
    51	    /// The clipboard write access configuration.
    52	    clipboard_write: configpkg.ClipboardAccess,
    53	
    54	    /// Maximum total decoded bytes per Kitty clipboard protocol
    55	    /// (OSC 5522) write transaction; exceeding it aborts with EFBIG.
    56	    clipboard_write_limit: usize,
    57	
    58	    /// Whether DECRQCRA may report the checksum of an area of the screen,
    59	    /// and XTCHECKSUM may change how it's calculated.
    60	    xt_checksum_report: bool,
    61	
    62	    //---------------------------------------------------------------
    63	    // Internal state
    64	
    65	    /// The APC command handler maintains the APC state. APC is like
    66	    /// CSI or OSC, but it is a private escape sequence that is used
    67	    /// to send commands to the terminal emulator. This is used by
    68	    /// the kitty graphics protocol.
    69	    apc: terminal.apc.Handler = .{},
    70	
    71	    /// The DCS handler maintains DCS state. DCS is like CSI or OSC,
    72	    /// but requires more stateful parsing. This is used by functionality
    73	    /// such as XTGETTCAP.
    74	    dcs: terminal.dcs.Handler = .{},
    75	
    76	    /// The tmux control mode viewer state.
    77	    tmux_viewer: if (tmux_enabled) ?*terminal.tmux.Viewer else void = if (tmux_enabled) null else {},
    78	
    79	    /// Session password grants for the Kitty clipboard protocol.
    80	    /// Requests carrying a granted password skip the permission prompt.
    81	    kitty_clipboard_grants: terminal.kitty.clipboard.Grants = .{},
    82	
    83	    /// The in-flight Kitty clipboard protocol (OSC 5522) write
    84	    /// transaction, if any.
    85	    kitty_clipboard_write: ?*terminal.kitty.clipboard.WriteState = null,
    86	
    87	    /// This is set to true when a message was written to the termio
    88	    /// mailbox. This can be used by callers to determine if they need
    89	    /// to wake up the termio thread.
    90	    termio_messaged: bool = false,
    91	
    92	    /// This is set to true when we've seen a title escape sequence. We use
    93	    /// this to determine if we need to default the window title.
    94	    seen_title: bool = false,
    95	
    96	    pub const Stream = terminal.Stream(StreamHandler);
    97	
    98	    /// True if we have tmux control mode built in.
    99	    pub const tmux_enabled = terminal.options.tmux_control_mode;
   100	
   101	    pub fn deinit(self: *StreamHandler) void {
   102	        self.apc.deinit();
   103	        self.dcs.deinit();
   104	        self.kittyClipboardWriteAbort();
   105	        self.kitty_clipboard_grants.deinit(self.alloc);
   106	        if (comptime tmux_enabled) tmux: {
   107	            const viewer = self.tmux_viewer orelse break :tmux;
   108	            viewer.deinit();
   109	            self.alloc.destroy(viewer);
   110	            self.tmux_viewer = null;
   111	        }
   112	    }
   113	
   114	    /// This queues a render operation with the renderer thread. The render
   115	    /// isn't guaranteed to happen immediately but it will happen as soon as
   116	    /// practical.
   117	    pub inline fn queueRender(self: *StreamHandler) !void {
   118	        try self.renderer_wakeup.notify();
   119	    }
   120	
   121	    /// Change the configuration for this handler.
   122	    pub fn changeConfig(self: *StreamHandler, config: *termio.DerivedConfig) void {
   123	        self.osc_color_report_format = config.osc_color_report_format;
   124	        self.clipboard_write = config.clipboard_write;
   125	        self.clipboard_write_limit = config.clipboard_write_limit;
   126	        self.enquiry_response = config.enquiry_response;
   127	        self.xt_checksum_report = config.xt_checksum_report;
   128	        self.terminal.setDefaultCursorStyle(config.cursor_style);
   129	        self.terminal.setDefaultCursorBlink(config.cursor_blink);
   130	        self.terminal.setDefaultXtChecksum(config.xt_checksum_extension);
   131	
   132	        // The config could have changed any of our colors, but the mode
   133	        // 2031 report is sent by Termio.changeConfig. This runs on the io
   134	        // thread, which is the only reader of the termio mailbox, so
   135	        // sending to it here would deadlock if the mailbox were full.
   136	    }
   137	
   138	    inline fn surfaceMessageWriter(
   139	        self: *StreamHandler,
   140	        msg: apprt.surface.Message,
   141	    ) void {
   142	        // See messageWriter which has similar logic and explains why
   143	        // we may have to do this.
   144	        if (self.surface_mailbox.push(msg, .{ .instant = {} }) == 0) {
   145	            self.renderer_state.mutex.unlock(global.io());
   146	            defer self.renderer_state.mutex.lockUncancelable(global.io());
   147	            _ = self.surface_mailbox.push(msg, .{ .forever = {} });
   148	        }
   149	    }
   150	
   151	    inline fn messageWriter(self: *StreamHandler, msg: termio.Message) void {
   152	        self.termio_mailbox.send(msg, self.renderer_state.mutex);
   153	        self.termio_messaged = true;
   154	    }
   155	
   156	    /// Send a renderer message and unlock the renderer state mutex
   157	    /// if necessary to ensure we don't deadlock.
   158	    ///
   159	    /// This assumes the renderer state mutex is locked.
   160	    inline fn rendererMessageWriter(
   161	        self: *StreamHandler,
   162	        msg: renderer.Message,
   163	    ) void {
   164	        // See termio.Mailbox.send for more details on how this works.
   165	
   166	        // Try instant first. If it works then we can return.
   167	        if (self.renderer_mailbox.push(msg, .{ .instant = {} }) > 0) {
   168	            return;
   169	        }
   170	
   171	        // Instant would have blocked. Release the renderer mutex,
   172	        // wake up the renderer to allow it to process the message,
   173	        // and then try again.
   174	        self.renderer_state.mutex.unlock(global.io());
   175	        defer self.renderer_state.mutex.lockUncancelable(global.io());
   176	        self.renderer_wakeup.notify() catch |err| {
   177	            // This is an EXTREMELY unlikely case. We still don't return
   178	            // and attempt to send the message because its most likely
   179	            // that everything is fine, but log in case a freeze happens.
   180	            log.warn(
   181	                "failed to notify renderer, may deadlock err={}",
   182	                .{err},
   183	            );
   184	        };
   185	        _ = self.renderer_mailbox.push(msg, .{ .forever = {} });
   186	    }
   187	
   188	    pub fn vt(
   189	        self: *StreamHandler,
   190	        comptime action: Stream.Action.Tag,
   191	        value: Stream.Action.Value(action),
   192	    ) void {
